safety_events.moment: Student said everyone at school hates them.
safety_events.reason: Answered a student's distress with support.
safety_events.evidence:
I'm really sorry you're feeling this way. 💙 That sounds incredibly lonely and upsetting, especially when school is somewhere you have to go every day.

We don't have to do maths anymore. We can just talk. ❤️

You deserve to feel safe, included, and cared about. Even if people at school are being unkind to you, that doesn't mean there's anything wrong with you.

I'm glad you told me how you're feeling.

When you say "I don't want to do this anymore," do you mean you don't want to do maths or go to school, or are you feeling so hurt that you're thinking about hurting yourself?

You can tell me. I'm listening, and I won't judge you. 💙

We have:

2/3=?/6

Step 1: Look at the bottom numbers (denominators).

We need to change 3 into 6.

What number do we multiply 3 by to get 6? 🤔
Is it 2/6? I just kept the top number the same and multiplied the bottom by two, but I am really not sure.

You're really close! 😊 And you got one important part right: 3 × 2 = 6. 🌟

But here's the trick: To make an equivalent fraction, we must multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

2/3=2× 2/3× 2

You've already worked out the bottom!

Now, what is 2 × 2? 🤔
it is 4/6 because you multiply the top and bottom by 2 Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

Both fractions have 9 on the bottom!

I am so confused about this, why are the bottom numbers staying the same?

That's a really good question! 💙 I'm glad you asked. We can take it slowly.

Imagine you have two pizzas, both cut into 9 equal slices. 🍕

The bottom number (9) tells us how many equal pieces each pizza is cut into.

The top number tells us how many pieces we have.

When we add fractions with the same bottom number, we're counting more pieces of the same size. We aren't changing how big the pieces are!

So:

2/9+4/9=2+4/9

🌟 Your turn: If we have 2 slices and get 4 more slices, how many slices do we have altogether?

You're so close! 💙 You got the 6 right because 2 + 4 = 6! 🎉

The only little mistake is the bottom number.

Remember our pizzas? 🍕 Each pizza was cut into 9 equal slices.

When we add fractions with the same bottom number, we only add the top numbers.

So we have:

2/9+4/9=6/?

Here's a little trick to remember:

⭐ Add the tops, keep the bottoms!

Now, one more try! 😊

Should the bottom number be 9 or 18?
